subject: SLO acceptance matrix and evaluation protocol
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Elaine Parker <elaine.parker@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: SLO acceptance matrix and evaluation protocol

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we move to a formal qualification run: 

1) Acceptance criteria (what BrightCart needs):
   - Latency: p95 target for short interactive prompts (<128 tokens) = 350ms or better
   - Streaming: graceful tail behavior, end-to-end p95 of streaming sessions <= 900ms (includes server send + client handling)
   - Concurrency/Throughput: steady 1,500 reqs/sec with bursts to 3,000 reqs/sec; pilot concurrency target = 200 concurrent sessions
   - Quality: exact prompt-response fidelity verified by the prompt-set eval (we'll compare model variants on the same prompt bundle)

2) What we need from BrightCart to run a reproducible benchmark:
   - Representative prompt set and the distribution (traffic profile) you want us to replay (sample + heavy tail).
   - Expected session duration distribution for streaming use cases (mean and 95th).
   - Any prefix-caching expectations (are there hot prefixes we should model as cached?)

3) Measurement rules we'll follow (draft; Ben will add formal definitions):
   - Compute p50/p95 on request-complete times per request type (stream vs non-stream), with warm-cache and cold-cache windows separated.
   - Report both per-request and per-session numbers for streaming flows.

4) Logistics / timeline:
   - If you can provide the prompt bundle + traffic CSV, we can schedule a 2-hour qualification window next week (we propose Oct 4-5).
   - We'll need IP allowlist + a temporary S3 location to push artifacts.

Attached: initial_prompt_bundle_v1.json (small sample) — please replace with your full set when you send it.

If this looks right I’ll coordinate a benchmark slot and share the measurement spec doc (Ben).

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Elaine Parker <elaine.parker@brightcart.com>

Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SLO acceptance matrix and evaluation protocol

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. Confirming BrightCart targets and attaching the sample artifacts: brightcart_prompt_samples_v2.json and traffic_profile_sep.csv. Key notes from our side: 

- Latency targets: p95 <= 350ms for short, non-streaming queries (<128 tokens). For streaming conversational flows we expect an end-to-end p95 <= 900ms (we understand streaming has different tail behavior).
- Concurrency/throughput: our production peak is ~3k reqs/sec, but for acceptance we want stable 1.5k reqs/sec with a concurrency test at 200 simultaneous interactive sessions.
- Streaming specifics: average session length ~18s, 95th=60s; typical tokens/sec = 25-35 depending on model size.
- Prefix caching: we do have hot prefixes (product name + SKU patterns) that account for ~12% of traffic; we can mark those in the traffic CSV.

We'll deliver the full prompt bundle and a full-day traffic trace by EOD Sep 30 (attached is a representative slice). We can also provide example client-side reconnection behavior if that helps.

Attached: brightcart_prompt_samples_v2.json, traffic_profile_sep.csv

Best,

BrightCart

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
Cc: Elaine Parker <elaine.parker@brightcart.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SLO acceptance matrix and evaluation protocol — measurement defs

Looping in the measurement details we discussed. Elaine — thanks for the artifacts, that helps a lot. A few clarifications and the definitions we'll use in the benchmark: 

- Measurement windows: we'll run two separate 2-hour windows (warm and steady-state) and report p50/p95/p99 per window. Warm window starts with a 15-minute ramp to populate KV cache for the hot prefixes; steady-state window follows.
- Request vs session: for streaming flows we'll record per-chunk latencies and compute session-complete times (time from first byte request to final byte received). All session metrics will be reported alongside per-chunk percentiles.
- Cold start accounting: any cold instances (defined as model container with no prior requests in last 5 minutes) will be excluded from steady-state p95 but reported separately.
- Prefix caching: we'll run runs both with prefix-caching enabled and disabled so you can see delta. The hot-prefix list from your CSV will be applied verbatim.
- Model variants: we will test two variants (baseline FP16 and quantized int8 fallback) and include correctness checks against the prompt set.

Attached: eval_harness_spec.md, measurement_definitions.md, benchmark_results_template.xlsx

Action for Marissa/Kim: I'll finalize the measurement spec and toss it into the Drive folder. We should also include a small sanity test (30 min) before the two-hour windows to validate network paths and allowlisting.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
